ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: The load shown in the figure absorbs 4 kW at a power factor of 0.89 lagging. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, the value of the reactance \(X\) to improve the input power factor to unity is ______.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a 50 Hz AC power source. The upper end of the power source passes through a series resistor labeled 1 Ω and then reaches the upper node. Between this node and the lower loop, a vertical reactance branch labeled X is connected in parallel, and it is also connected to the primary side of an ideal transformer. Beside the transformer, the turns ratio is labeled as 2:1, and the secondary side on the right is connected to the load ZL, with the secondary-side voltage marked as 110 V. Reasoning: The load absorbs active power P = 4 kW, and the power factor is 0.89 lagging, so the inductive reactive power of the load is QL = P tan(cos^-1(0.89)). Calculating gives tan(cos^-1(0.89)) = sqrt(1 - 0.89^2) / 0.89 ≈ 0.5123, so QL ≈ 4000 × 0.5123 = 2049 VAR. The turns ratio of the ideal transformer is 2:1, and the secondary-side voltage is 110 V, so the primary-side voltage Vp = 2 × 110 = 220 V. X is connected in parallel with the primary side of the transformer, so the voltage across X is 220 V. To make the input power factor unity, X should provide capacitive reactive power equal in magnitude and opposite in direction to the load reactive power, namely QX = -QL. Thus |X| = Vp^2 / QL = 220^2 / 2049 ≈ 23.61 Ω. Therefore, the magnitude of the required reactance is 23.61 Ω, and its nature is capacitive.

raw_record.question_text: The load shown in the figure absorbs 4 kW at a power factor of 0.89 lagging. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, the value of the reactance \(X\) to improve the input power factor to unity is ______.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: a 50 Hz source feeds a 1 ohm series resistor, then a node where X is in parallel with the primary of an ideal 2:1 transformer; the secondary has 110 V across load ZL. From the text, take the load power as P=4 kW at pf=0.89 lagging. Compute the load reactive power QL=P tan(cos^-1 0.89). Using the 2:1 ideal transformer and 110 V secondary voltage, get the primary voltage Vp=220 V. Because X is across the primary, choose it to provide capacitive reactive power QX=-QL, so |X|=Vp^2/QL. This gives approximately 23.61 ohms, with capacitive sign if sign convention is requested.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中左侧是 50 Hz 交流电源，电源上端经过一个标注为 1 Ω 的串联电阻后到达上方节点。该节点与下方回路之间并联接有一个标注为 X 的竖直 reactance 支路，同时也接到理想变压器的一次侧。变压器旁标注匝比为 2:1，右侧二次侧接负载 ZL，并标出二次侧电压为 110 V。推理：负载吸收有功功率 P = 4 kW，功率因数为 0.89 滞后，因此负载感性无功功率为 QL = P tan(cos^-1(0.89))。计算得 tan(cos^-1(0.89)) = sqrt(1 - 0.89^2) / 0.89 ≈ 0.5123，所以 QL ≈ 4000 × 0.5123 = 2049 VAR。理想变压器匝比为 2:1，二次侧电压为 110 V，因此一次侧电压 Vp = 2 × 110 = 220 V。X 与变压器一次侧并联，所以 X 两端电压为 220 V。为使输入功率因数为 unity，X 应提供与负载无功大小相等、方向相反的容性无功，即 QX = -QL。于是 |X| = Vp^2 / QL = 220^2 / 2049 ≈ 23.61 Ω。因此所需 reactance 的大小为 23.61 Ω，性质为容性。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct complex-power/power-factor-correction route: it uses the transformer voltage ratio to move the given load power to the primary side and sizes the shunt reactance by reactive-power cancellation.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the figure that the ideal transformer has a 2:1 turns ratio, the secondary/load voltage is 110 V, the unknown reactance X is connected in shunt across the transformer primary, and a 1 ohm resistor is in series with the source before that shunt/primary node.
planner_metadata.text_role: Read from the question that the load absorbs 4 kW at 0.89 lagging power factor, the transformer is ideal, and the goal is to make the input power factor unity.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use ideal-transformer relations to get the primary voltage from the secondary voltage; use Q=P tan(cos^-1 pf) for the lagging load reactive power; for unity input power factor, the shunt reactance must supply equal and opposite reactive power. Since the 1 ohm element is purely resistive, after reactive cancellation it does not affect the required reactive compensation.
